design_intent.original_text: Convert this complete 2D Tic-Tac-Toe game into a playable 3D Tic-Tac-Toe game.
preserve: The source game's identity as Tic-Tac-Toe.
changes: Convert the existing 2D game into a playable 3D Tic-Tac-Toe game.
constraints: Do not assume board dimensions, winning conditions, or interaction details not specified by the request.
unresolved: The 3D board dimensions and layout are unspecified.
The intended 3D winning conditions are unspecified.
The desired controls and 3D presentation are unspecified.

value.title: 3D Tic Tac Toe
value.description: A 3×3×3 spatial lift of the source game. X and O alternate; three matching marks on a straight spatial line win. A full board without a winner draws.

value.name: Local player controlling both alternating marks

variables.name: Board cell: empty, X or O

value.name: Detect three matching marks on a straight spatial line
Detect a full volume without a winner
Alternate marks unless the game ended
Complete three of your marks on a straight line through the volume
Current mark is X or O

assumptions: The requested 3D conversion adds three depth layers while retaining the source’s three-cell line length and alternating marks.
The registered grid.has_line function evaluates straight lines across all axes and diagonals of a rank-3 rectangular topology.

Full-session restart and quit are host commands, not Rule actions; the input stage must route R to host_command restart and Escape to host_command quit. Existing scene and input documents require corresponding spatial-lift updates.

value.title: 3D Tic Tac Toe
value.description: One centered 3×3×3 volume with selectable slate-coloured cell shells, blue X marks, amber O marks, and the source game's status and control text.

value.name: Turn status unless a mark wins
Turn status unless the board is drawn

properties.text: Click an empty cell. R: restart. Esc: quit.

value.name: Show empty, X or O at each site

assumptions: The engine-owned spatial layout supplies the volume overview camera and omits the source's flat screen backdrop from the spatial viewport.
One world unit represents the source's 140-pixel cell pitch; negative world Y preserves the source's downward row order.

value.title: 3D Tic Tac Toe
value.description: The source draws its board, X and O marks, and colours procedurally; it uses Pygame’s bundled default font for status and instructions. No project image, audio or model files are required.
